solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Clouts cast by insect

indicators.note: cast in the sense of thrown about or moulded anew, so the letters of clouts are reshaped

explanation.surface: Someone throws punches at a bug.
explanation.definitionFit: A locust is a swarming grasshopper, a familiar example of an insect.

clue.text: Permission to quit

definitions.meaning: consent, as in being granted time off
to depart or go away from a place

explanation.surface: Being allowed to resign.
explanation.definitionFit: Leave is both a noun for permission and a verb meaning to go away.

clue.text: Cold part of Italy — or of England?

definitions.note: read with the preceding 'part': or part of England

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
Umbria is a central Italian region

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a chilly region is in Italy or England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part' does double duty, supplying the definition's 'part of England'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cumbria is a county in north-west England, home of the Lake District.

clue.text: Desperate to get out of ritzy cars

indicators.note: the letters are pulled out of their arrangement and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Someone longing to escape from flashy vehicles.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is close to all-in-one: being stuck in 'ritzy cars' would make anyone want out.
explanation.definitionFit: Stir-crazy describes someone frantic from confinement, desperate to escape.

clue.text: Cut around page featuring prominent headline

indicators.note: the word for cut goes around the page letter, enclosing it

parts.note: to cut is to slash

explanation.surface: An editor trims a page that carries a big headline.
explanation.definitionFit: In journalism a splash is the main front-page story with its banner headline.

clue.text: Eradicate source of pruritis (itch)

indicators.note: the source of a word is where it begins, its first letter

parts.note: an itch is a craving, an urge

explanation.surface: Getting rid of the cause of an itchy skin condition.
explanation.definitionFit: To purge is to rid or cleanse completely, so it means to eradicate.

clue.text: One in Thames struggling with unbelief

indicators.note: the letter for one sits inside the reworked river
struggling suggests flailing about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone floundering in the Thames, wrestling with a loss of faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'struggling' rearranges THAMES into ATHESM, and the I goes between E and S.
explanation.definitionFit: Atheism is the lack of belief in any god, so it is a form of unbelief.

clue.text: Clown Prince unbounded, one of five

indicators.note: with its boundaries gone, so the first and last letters go

parts.note: Charles, long Britain's Prince of Wales
a quin is one of quintuplets, five born together

explanation.surface: A royal jester running loose with four companions.
explanation.definitionFit: Harlequin is the masked comic servant of pantomime, a stock clown figure.

clue.text: Froth of liquor giving succour to one who serves it

parts.note: barm is the yeasty froth on fermenting malt liquor
succour means help, aid

explanation.surface: Beer froth seems to be comforting someone pulling pints.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman working behind a pub counter serves the liquor, so she is the one who serves it.

clue.text: Where to grow fruit or vegetable

parts.note: chard is a leafy vegetable

explanation.surface: A gardener's choice: a fruit plot or a vegetable patch.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchard is a planted area of fruit trees, the place where fruit is grown.

clue.text: Sweetheart, conceited, holds fast to sweetheart

indicators.note: the conceited word holds the fast inside it

parts.note: vain means conceited
Lent is the Christian period of fasting
the heart of the word sweet is its middle letter E

explanation.surface: A vain lover clings tightly to a partner.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'sweetheart' is read as sweet-heart, the middle of 'sweet'.
explanation.definitionFit: A valentine is a person chosen as one's beloved on 14 February.

clue.text: Speak ill of one taken in by decrease in value

indicators.note: the letter for one is absorbed into the word for speak ill of

parts.note: to deprecate is to disparage or speak ill of
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Criticising something whose worth is falling.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface hints both near-twin verbs mean the same; adding I to one turns it into the other.
explanation.definitionFit: To depreciate is to lose worth over time, as cars and currencies do.

clue.text: Couple I bumped into on the way back

indicators.note: travelling backwards, so the word for bumped into is read from right to left

parts.note: to bump into someone is to meet them

explanation.surface: Someone recalls a pair they ran into on the return journey.
explanation.definitionFit: An item is informal for a romantic pair, two people going out together.

clue.text: Play with a tot first

indicators.note: first says the word for tot comes before the a

parts.note: a tot is a small drink, a dram

explanation.surface: A theatre outing begins with a quick nip of whisky.
explanation.definitionFit: A drama is a stage work, a play performed by actors.

clue.text: Incomplete farce maybe turned titillating — it gives people what they asked for!

definitions.text: it gives people what they asked for!

indicators.note: turned around, so the shortened comic genre is read backwards
not finished, so the last letter is cut

parts.note: farce is one kind of comedy
racy means titillating or risqué

explanation.surface: A cut-short saucy farce, then a wry remark on giving audiences what they want.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Incomplete' trims COMEDY to COMED; 'turned' makes it DEMOC.
explanation.definitionFit: Government by the people delivers whatever the voters elect, for better or worse.

clue.text: Plaudit for commune I reformed

indicators.note: formed again in a new arrangement, so the letters are rebuilt

explanation.surface: Someone earns praise for reorganising their collective farm.
explanation.definitionFit: An encomium is a formal tribute or speech of high praise, a plaudit.

clue.text: About to get rich without initially running to fat

parts.note: C is short for circa, about

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so rich surrounds the letter

parts.note: opulent means wealthy, rich

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of running

explanation.surface: Someone about to get wealthy without effort grows plump.
explanation.definitionFit: Corpulent means stout or overweight, a formal synonym for fat.

clue.text: Drug being injected, stay Rolling Stone (of sorts)

indicators.note: the drug is put inside the other letters, as a needle puts it into a vein
rolling about, so the letters of stay are tumbled

parts.note: meth is short for methamphetamine

explanation.surface: A drug user injecting while staying with the Rolling Stones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rolling Stone' suggests the band, but 'Rolling' is the anagram signal giving AYST, and the stone is a gem.
explanation.definitionFit: An amethyst is a purple quartz gemstone, a precious stone of sorts.

clue.text: Flashlight illuminating dishcloth?

parts.note: a torch is the British word for a flashlight
a light that is illuminating is switched on

explanation.surface: Shining a flashlight on a tea towel.
explanation.definitionFit: Torchon is French for a kitchen cloth, also a coarse lace; the question mark flags the foreign term.

clue.text: Endlessly dressing bird

indicators.note: without its end, so the last letter of the word for dressing goes

parts.note: robing is putting on robes, dressing

explanation.surface: A bird forever preening and grooming itself.
explanation.definitionFit: The robin is a common small songbird with a red breast.

clue.text: Bird giving name to beer

indicators.note: to says the name letter is attached to the end of the beer

parts.note: bitter is a British style of hoppy draught ale

explanation.surface: A bird has a beer named after it.
explanation.definitionFit: The bittern is a wading heron of reedbeds, known for its booming call.

clue.text: Relic of damage to cliff

definitions.meaning: a mark left behind after a wound has healed
a steep rock face or crag on a hillside

explanation.surface: Erosion has left its mark on a cliff face.
explanation.definitionFit: A scar is both the mark a healed wound leaves and a craggy rock face on a hillside.

clue.text: Advisor finding new ruler in bed

indicators.note: the new ruler lies inside the bed

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
a sultan is a Muslim ruler

explanation.surface: A specialist discovers a freshly crowned monarch tucked up in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A consultant is a professional hired to give expert advice.

clue.text: Waste matter and energy, lacking refinement

parts.note: crud is filth or waste matter
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Sewage and power, both unprocessed.
explanation.definitionFit: Crude means rough and unpolished, as crude oil is unrefined.

clue.text: Loud part of casino is yours

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A croupier telling a winner the gaming house now belongs to them.
explanation.definitionFit: Noisy means making a lot of sound, a synonym for loud.

clue.text: Be in centre, keeping time — be in hot water here?

parts.note: in cricket a batsman who is in is batting, so be in means bat

indicators.note: the word for centre holds the time letter within it

parts.note: a hub is a centre

explanation.surface: Instructions for staying central and punctual, then a quip about trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the batsman currently batting is 'in'. 'Be in hot water' usually means trouble; here it is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: A tub is where you literally sit in hot water while bathing; the question mark flags the pun.

clue.text: Dissenter causing present convulsion

parts.note: present means here, in attendance
a tic is an involuntary spasm

explanation.surface: A rebel triggers a current upheaval.
explanation.definitionFit: A heretic holds views at odds with accepted doctrine, so dissents from it.

clue.text: Left number — unspecified number — back over there

indicators.note: back says the whole string is read in reverse

parts.note: red is used for a left-wing socialist
Y is an algebraic unknown, an unspecified number

explanation.surface: Someone left a number behind back there.
explanation.definitionFit: Yonder is an old-fashioned word for over there, at a distance.

clue.text: Mean fish sun-god's eradicated

indicators.note: wiped out, so the god's name is removed from the fish

parts.note: a stingray is a flat fish
Ra is the Egyptian sun god; 's is short for is

explanation.surface: A cruel fish has wiped out a deity.
explanation.definitionFit: Stingy means ungenerous or miserly, the sense of mean with money.
